first_impression.reaction: Sophie sent this with 'Mum, this is who I was telling you about for the honeymoon.' The honeymoon is really their business, not mine, but I suspect some of the bill will find its way to us. The second sentence is the one that kept me reading: 'The good ones agree their fee and confirm what is included in writing before you commit to anything.' Sensible, plain and no slang. I'll read it properly.

journey.quote: The good ones agree their fee and confirm what is included in writing before you commit to anything.
journey.reaction: Good. Fee and inclusions in writing, right at the top this time. That's what I want to see before anyone pays anything.

journey.quote: Decide your dates, length, style and must-haves first, then ask any planner about fees, inclusions, terms, insurance, exchange rates and commissions.
journey.reaction: Commissions! Nobody ever mentions those. It reads as though they expect to be asked hard questions and don't mind.

journey.section: What a planner does for your honeymoon
journey.quote: Each piece comes with its own deposit, its own deadline and its own terms.
journey.reaction: Exactly my worry, put plainly. Lots of little deposits to lots of different people overseas. I'm glad someone is keeping them in step, but it does make me ask who holds the money.

journey.section: What a planner does for your honeymoon
journey.quote: You give up none of your rights by handing the trip to someone else.
journey.reaction: A clear, short sentence on consumer rights. Much easier on the iPad than the usual legal paragraph.

journey.section: How it works with Wedded Wonderland
journey.quote: So on cost, you know the fee, in writing, before anything happens.
journey.reaction: It said this in the sentence just before. Saying it twice in a row makes it sound like they're trying a little too hard to convince me.

journey.section: How it works with Wedded Wonderland
journey.quote: Your advisor works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: AUD and Melbourne hours. That's what I need. Still no name for the advisor, and nothing about who answers the phone once they've actually flown out.

journey.quote: Born in Australia and married overseas? You will always need a name change certificate for your passport.
journey.reaction: Now that's practical. I would never have thought of it, and it's the kind of thing that ruins a trip at the airport. I'll make sure Sophie reads this bit.

journey.section: What to decide before you enquire
journey.quote: Think about how you would like to pay, in what order and on what card, before the first deposit is due.
journey.reaction: Very sensible, and exactly the conversation Geoff and I need to have with the girls. I'd have liked a word here about deposits being protected too, but I see the questions section deals with that.

journey.section: Questions to ask any planner before you agree
journey.quote: These are worth asking whoever you speak to, including us.
journey.reaction: 'Including us.' I like that. It doesn't make me feel old-fashioned for wanting to ask.

journey.section: Questions to ask any planner before you agree
journey.quote: Agent insolvency is commonly excluded from cancellation cover, and insolvency insurance is not compulsory for agents, so only some have it.
journey.reaction: This is the one that keeps me up at night. I'm glad it's said straight. Naturally I now want to know whether Wedded Wonderland holds it, and the page doesn't say.

journey.section: Questions to ask any planner before you agree
journey.quote: Ask whether the rate is guaranteed, what fees or margin apply and whether the receiver pays anything at the other end.
journey.reaction: Geoff will love this. He always says the bank's rate is where they get you.

journey.quote: A fee only means something next to what it covers.
journey.reaction: True enough, but as an answer to 'How much does it cost?' it feels like a polite dodge. I understand they can't put a figure here, but I'd rather be told that plainly.

journey.quote: With one Wedded Advisor from the first conversation to the flight home, the fee agreed in writing before any work begins and the inclusions confirmed in writing before you commit, it can be.
journey.reaction: A good summary. 'To the flight home' is reassuring, though I'd want to hear on the phone what that means if something goes wrong while they're away.

unanswered_questions: Who would the Wedded Advisor be, by name, and can I speak to them on the phone before anything is booked?
Who do Sophie and James ring if something goes wrong at 2am wherever they are?
How is the Wedded Wonderland fee worked out, and roughly what does it come to for a two-week honeymoon?
Does Wedded Wonderland hold insolvency insurance, and who holds the deposits paid to overseas hotels?
Does Wedded Wonderland receive commission from the hotels and airlines, as well as the fee?
Does 'speak with Wedded Concierge' mean a phone call or an online form?
would_share_with: My husband Geoff, with the seven questions to ask any planner, especially the exchange rate and commission ones
Sophie, with the passport and name change section

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [speak with Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=honeymoon-planning-service&utm_content=closing) and tell us anything.
cta_reaction.why: 'Speak with' sounds like a person, which is what I want. It's the couple's decision to make, so I'd more likely send it to Sophie with my list of questions than click it myself. If it's a phone call, I'd be happy to be on it.

top_3_changes: Remove 'So on cost, you know the fee, in writing, before anything happens.' It repeats the sentence before it word for word in meaning and makes the reassurance sound forced.
In 'Pace of payment', add a short pointer to the insolvency and travel insurance questions further down, so the person thinking about deposits sees straight away that protecting them is covered.

Make the 'How much does a honeymoon planner cost?' answer more direct: say plainly that the fee depends on the trip and is quoted in writing before any work begins, rather than opening with a general remark that reads like a dodge.
